description:
The documented polynomial of the canonical $\mathrm{GF}(2^8)$ field disagrees with the one the code builds, so callers matching gf2 against AES or byte-field libraries read the wrong field from the documentation.

## Background

The rustdoc of `Gf2mField::gf256()` in `crates/gf2-core/src/gf2m/field.rs` names the modulus $x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1$ and calls it the field used in AES. The constructor builds modulus `0b100011101`, which is $x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + 1$ (0x11D); the AES field uses $x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1$ (0x11B). In `crates/gf2-core/src/primitive_polys.rs`, the degree-8 entry of the standard primitive-polynomial table carries the same 0x11D value with a comment calling the five-term polynomial a trinomial. The two fields are not isomorphic under the identity map, so a comparison or interoperability claim built on the documentation compares different arithmetic.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The public documentation of `Gf2mField::gf256()` states the modulus the constructor builds and attributes to it only applications that use that modulus.
- [hard] REQ-02: The degree-8 entry of the standard primitive-polynomial table is described by its actual term count and polynomial.
- [hard] REQ-03: A doctest or unit test checks the documented `gf256()` modulus against the field the constructor returns, so the two cannot diverge silently.

## Notes

Surfaced by the protocol-v3 byte-field comparison survey while establishing which $\mathrm{GF}(2^8)$ polynomial each gf2 type uses against external byte-field libraries.
title: Document the GF(2^8) polynomial that gf256() builds
